words.trick: Feasible sounds like 'fees-able'; if you pay fees, admission is possible.

words.en: inspiring fear or respect through being large or powerful
words.ex: The competitive exam presents a formidable challenge to most students every year.
words.trick: Think of a devil in your 'form'; it would be very scary.

words.en: to suffer through a difficult situation without giving up
words.ex: Farmers in the village had to endure a long and harsh summer.
words.trick: Endure is like 'end-sure'; staying sure until the very end.

words.en: the capacity to withstand hardship or long-term stress
words.ex: Long distance running requires great physical and mental endurance.
words.trick: Endurance is your 'inner-stamina' to reach the finish line.

words.en: to draw out a reaction or information from someone
words.bn: বের করা, আদায় করা, প্রকাশ করা
words.ex: The lawyer tried to elicit a confession from the witness during questioning.
words.trick: Elicit sounds like 'explicit'; trying to get an explicit response.

tr.mr: ओढून काढणे, निष्पन्न करणे, बाहेर काढणे
tr.ta: வெளியே கொணர், பெற முயல், வெளிப்படுத்தச் செய்
tr.gu: ખેંચી કાઢવું, બહાર લાવવું, પ્રેરિત કરવું
tr.or: ବାହାର କରିବା, ଆଦାୟ କରିବା, ପ୍ରକାଶ କରିବା
tr.as: উলিয়াই অনা, প্ৰকাশ কৰা, টানি উসলোৱা

words.en: existing as a natural and permanent quality of something
words.ex: Every job carries an inherent risk of stress that workers must manage carefully.
words.trick: Think of 'in-here-ent': a quality that stays deep in here permanently.

words.en: originating or occurring naturally in a particular place
words.ex: India relies on indigenous technology to design affordable space exploration missions.
words.trick: Indi-genous sounds like India-generates, meaning produced locally.

words.en: a sudden strong wish or urge to act
words.ex: She controlled her impulse to buy expensive clothes during the festive shopping sale.
words.trick: Impulse is like an inner pulse that drives a sudden reaction.

words.en: belonging naturally to the essential nature of something
words.ex: A student's intrinsic motivation leads to consistent long-term academic progress.
words.trick: Intrinsic starts with 'in-', referring to what lies inside the core.

words.en: to hinder, restrain, or prevent an action or process
words.ex: Fear of failure should not inhibit students from attempting challenging exam problems.
words.trick: Inhibit sounds like prohibit, which means to hinder or stop something.

tr.as: বাধা দিয়া, ৰোধ কৰা, নিৰোধ কৰা

words.en: a natural tendency or preference toward something
words.ex: Rohan showed a strong inclination toward mathematics from an early age.
words.trick: Think of leaning in a direction, like an incline or slope.

words.en: very complicated or detailed in design or structure
words.ex: The saree features intricate embroidery crafted carefully by traditional weavers.
words.trick: Sounds like in-trick-art, a detailed art piece full of tricks.

words.en: lacking the power or ability to move or act
words.ex: The patient lay inert on the bed until the medicine took effect.
words.trick: Connect with inertia, which means remaining still without moving.

words.en: a formal accusation or charge of a serious crime
words.ex: The panel issued a severe indictment against the corrupt committee members.
words.trick: In-dict means to dictate a formal legal charge against someone.

words.en: to make someone extremely angry or enraged
words.ex: The unexpected hike in bus fares will incense daily commuters.
words.trick: Like burning incense sticks, anger fumes up intensely.

words.en: standing out so as to be easily seen or famous
words.ex: A prominent billboard near the station displays the new college admission details.
words.trick: Pro-minute: something so big it is noticed every minute.

words.en: having great depth, insight, or intense impact
words.ex: The speaker's profound words on ethics left the students thinking for hours.
words.trick: Pro-found: a professional finds deep meanings in everything.

words.en: related to a small region or having a narrow outlook
words.ex: Students often struggle to shed their provincial mindset when moving to metro cities.
words.trick: Province-ial: limited only to one's own province or village.

words.en: the beginning of something, especially something unpleasant
words.ex: The onset of the monsoon brings relief from the scorching summer heat.
words.trick: On-set: when the crew is on set, the filming starts.

words.en: respect or admiration earned through achievement or status
words.ex: Getting into a top university carries immense prestige in Indian families.
words.trick: Press-stage: being on stage with the press watching gives you status.

words.en: a standard model or typical example of something
words.ex: The government launched a new paradigm for rural healthcare development across India.
words.trick: Parad-Igm sounds like Pair of Design - a standard design to follow.

words.en: a situation that seems self-contradictory but is true
words.ex: It is a paradox that the busiest cities often have the loneliest people.
words.trick: Para-Dox: Para means opposite and Dox means opinion; opposite to common logic.

words.en: existing commonly or widely accepted in a particular area
words.ex: Digital payments are now prevalent even in small villages across India.
words.trick: Pre-valent: Pre means before and valent means value; something having value everywhere.

words.en: relevant or directly related to the matter at hand
words.ex: The candidate asked many pertinent questions during the campus interview.
words.trick: Per-ti-nent: Think of pertaining to the net result or relevant.

words.en: a first preliminary version of a machine or design
words.ex: Indian engineers are testing a prototype of a new electric car for urban roads.
words.trick: Proto-Type: Proto means first and Type means model; the first model.

words.en: arranged for the present time but likely to be changed
words.ex: The university released a provisional merit list before the final seat allotment.
words.trick: Think of a provision made for now that might change later.

words.en: the outer edge or boundary of an area
words.ex: Many small tea stalls are located on the periphery of the campus.
words.trick: Peri means around, like the outer boundary of a circle.

words.en: more important than anything else
words.ex: For a pilot, the safety of passengers is of paramount importance.
words.trick: Paramount sounds like a mountain peak, which is at the top.

words.en: showing strong support for one side or party
words.ex: The committee took a partisan approach instead of reviewing the facts objectively.
words.trick: Focusing only on one part or side of the story.

words.en: spreading widely throughout an area or group of people
words.ex: Mobile technology has a pervasive influence on the lives of Indian youth.
words.trick: Think of a perfume pervading every corner of a room.

tr.ur: ہر جگہ پھیلا ہوا، همہ گیر

words.en: a thing that comes before and signals something else
words.ex: A mild fever is often a precursor to a more severe illness.
words.trick: The prefix 'pre' means before; a precursor is like a runner who goes before.

words.en: a dangerous, difficult, or otherwise unfortunate situation
words.ex: The plight of street animals during the monsoon is truly heartbreaking.
words.trick: Rhymes with light; when you are in a plight, you look for the light.

words.en: to deliberately make someone feel angry or annoyed
words.ex: Do not provoke the stray dogs while they are eating.
words.trick: Pro (forward) + voke (vocal); it is like calling out to start a fight.

words.en: not able to be seen through; not transparent
words.ex: The office cabin has opaque glass windows for privacy.
words.trick: Sounds like 'O-pack'; a pack that is so thick light cannot pass through.

words.en: a person authorized to act on behalf of another
words.ex: He asked his friend to sign the attendance sheet as his proxy.
words.trick: A proxy acts 'pro' (for) 'you' (represented by the 'y').

words.en: dangerously unstable or likely to fall or collapse
words.ex: The daily wage laborer lives in a precarious financial situation due to irregular work.
words.trick: Pre-care-us: Take care before walking on an unstable path that might collapse.

words.en: a natural tendency to behave in a particular way
words.ex: My younger brother has a propensity for eating spicy street food every evening.
words.trick: Pro-pen-sity: A professional writer has a natural tendency to use a pen.

words.en: to prevent something from happening or make it impossible
words.bn: নিবারণ করা, বাধা দেওয়া, অসম্ভব করা
words.ex: A serious knee injury might preclude the athlete from participating in the next Olympics.
words.trick: Pre-exclude: To exclude something beforehand is to preclude its occurrence.

words.en: a difficult, unpleasant, or embarrassing situation
words.ex: Rahul found himself in a predicament when he forgot his wallet before paying the bill.
words.trick: Pre-dict-ment: A situation so bad you cannot predict the way out.

words.en: behavior that is socially acceptable and follows conventional standards
words.ex: The guest followed every rule of propriety during the traditional wedding ceremony.
words.trick: Sounds like 'proper-ty' which implies acting in a proper and polite way.

words.en: to assume something is true as a basis for reasoning
words.ex: Economic theories often postulate that people act logically to maximize their profit.
words.trick: Think of a 'post-it' note where you stick a starting idea to build on.

words.en: an unintentional failure to notice or do something correctly
words.ex: Due to a clerical oversight, the invitation was sent to the wrong department.
words.trick: You look 'over' the detail instead of looking at it, so you miss it.

words.en: intended as a punishment or involving very high costs
words.ex: High punitive taxes were imposed to discourage the consumption of harmful goods.
words.trick: Punitive sounds exactly like the root word 'punish'.

words.en: of crucial importance in relation to a final result
words.ex: Hard work plays a pivotal role in clearing the civil services examination.
words.trick: A 'pivot' is a central point around which everything else turns.

words.en: a special right or privilege held by a specific group
words.ex: The captain used his prerogative to choose the batting order for the match.
words.trick: A prerogative is like a 'Pre-Right' - a right you have before anyone else.

words.en: causing great harm or damage in a subtle way
words.ex: Excessive screen time has a pernicious effect on the eyesight of young children.
words.trick: Pernicious sounds like vicious, which describes something harmful and evil.

words.en: not aware of what is happening around oneself
words.ex: She was so absorbed in her work that she was oblivious of the noise.
words.trick: Oblivious sounds like 'obvious' - you are missing what is obvious to others.

words.en: to make the most effective use of something
words.ex: A good strategy will help you optimize your time during the entrance exam.
words.trick: Think of the word 'Optimum', which means the best possible level.

words.en: exceptional skill or ability in a particular activity
words.ex: Indian engineers are known worldwide for their technical prowess and innovation.
words.trick: Prowess sounds like being 'proud of success' due to your great skill.

words.en: To think about something carefully for a long time.
words.ex: Students often ponder over their career choices after the board results are announced.
words.trick: Ponder sounds like pond; imagine sitting by a quiet pond thinking deeply.

words.en: Remarkably or impressively great in extent, size, or degree.
words.ex: The young musician showed prodigious talent by winning three national awards in a year.
words.trick: Prodigious sounds like Proud plus Enormous; something so big it makes you proud.

words.en: Evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret.
words.ex: The movie's poignant ending left the entire audience in tears at the local cinema.
words.trick: Poignant contains the sound of pain; it refers to things causing emotional pain.

words.en: In its original condition; clean and fresh as if new.
words.ex: The trekkers were amazed to see the pristine beauty of the Himalayan landscape.
words.trick: Pristine sounds like Priest; think of a priest's clean and pure white robes.

words.en: A preference or special liking for something.
words.ex: Ramesh has a predilection for spicy street food despite his doctor's warnings.
words.trick: Pre-election; voters have a preference for a candidate before the election starts.
